outcome: Legendre's conjecture remains unproven; nothing found since 26 January 2024 changes what a careful person would write in this entry.
summary: No result since 26 January 2024 changes the status of Legendre's conjecture, and no AI system is credited with anything relevant to it. Three lines of activity were found. (1) Computational verification: Sorenson and Webster's algorithm paper (arXiv:2401.13753, submitted 24 Jan 2024, two days before the frozen revision) extended the verified range of the underlying Oppermann's-conjecture search from N=2e9 to N=3.33e13; the published version (Research in Number Theory, 2025) reports a further extension to N=7.05e13 using a classical parallel sieve algorithm on Xeon Phi/Xeon E5 clusters — no AI or machine learning of any kind. Per the deep-dive rule for existence questions (§3.1), extending a verified range narrows where a counterexample could hide but does not answer the existence question, so this is not a status-changing event regardless of its date, which in any case falls right at or before the window boundary. (2) An unaccepted preprint claim: arXiv:2403.08306 (Li and Li, submitted 13 March 2024, revised through v3 on 20 March 2024) claims a full proof via a coprime-density argument. It has no journal acceptance, no expert digestion, no citations building on it as a settled result, and general number-theory practice treats such elementary coprime-counting arguments for Legendre's conjecture with strong skepticism given the problem's difficulty; it does not meet the bar for `claimed` in the sense the schema intends (a status a careful expert would take seriously), so it is noted here rather than elevating the record's status. Other self-published claims (academia.edu, viXra, an 'Oriental Journal' venue) were also found and carry no weight. (3) Genuine but conditional related progress: Chamberland and Straub, 'Weakening the Legendre Conjecture' (arXiv:2602.22502, submitted 26 Feb 2026), is a legitimate paper by established mathematicians showing that, assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, a recent result implies existence of primes between x^(2+δ) and (x+1)^(2+δ) for δ≥1/4, with explicit computational bounds for smaller δ. This is scope-excluded under §3.1: it changes the exponent from 2 to 2+δ, which is a different (weaker) question, not a restriction of the stated problem to a special case, so it is a related problem rather than a case of Legendre's conjecture and does not move this record's status even though it is real, RH-conditional progress on the neighboring question. No AI involvement was found or claimed anywhere in this cluster of results.
competing_reading: One could argue the Sorenson-Webster range extension, since its arXiv preprint predates the frozen revision by only two days but its peer-reviewed journal publication (2025) and largest reported figure (7.05e13) postdate it, should be recorded as a dated 'progress' event under the paper's later publication kind. I did not do this because §6.3 requires dating by the first public written argument (the January 2024 preprint), and in any case §3.1 excludes range-extension results from counting as movement on an existence question at all, so no event exists to date regardless of which the paper's version is used.
what_would_settle_it: A full proof or explicit counterexample accepted by expert digestion or a journal of record; alternatively, an unconditional (non-RH) proof of the weakened exponent-2 statement, or a credible expert review elevating one of the preprint proof claims (arXiv:2403.08306 or similar) to serious consideration.
